description:
FOUNDATION. Derive, for every first-class callable value, a CallConvention: Typed(arg_reprs, return_repr) when the value has a single concrete uniform surface (all join arms share one arg/return representation), or Boxed otherwise (heterogeneous arms, or the value flows to a position whose type erases the convention to any/ValueRef). Record it on the callable's transport facts. This is the discriminator the whole epic turns on; it must be exactly right.

WHY: representation must follow convention. A phi of same-signature fn-refs has a known convention even though it has no single identity; the surface IS the convention. The surfaces are already propagated by the callable-flow (CallableFlowFact); this ticket reads them and classifies.

WHAT: a derivation over the per-executable callable-flow facts + the apply-site surfaces. Typed iff exactly one concrete surface (arity + grounded arg/return reprs) covers all arms; Boxed iff surfaces diverge or are absent/opaque. Subsumes the phantom-surface concern (fz-rh2.29.7): a Typed convention requires ONE concrete surface, so a polymorphic template surface alongside a concrete sibling must already be gone (retain_most_specific is the same rule, now load-bearing for classification). The surface's RETURN must be the grounded concrete return (this is where the old fault-3 'boundary return is polymorphic' dissolves -- the convention carries int, not alpha).

NO BEHAVIOR CHANGE yet. Pure fact + telemetry.

CHECK: a focused test asserts the convention fact for the corpus -- reducer in opaque_fn_value_join -> Typed[(RawInt,RawInt)->RawInt]; a genuinely opaque/heterogeneous callable -> Boxed; the single-ref reducer (00178) -> Typed; grounded provider callbacks (destructors) unaffected. cargo test --lib green, zero warnings.
title: Classify each first-class callable's calling convention as a transport fact
